text:
Trap one: credit. In Wonga's survey, more than one in five people planned to use credit for the festive season. A store card or a buy-now-pay-later plan feels free in December, but the first payment arrives in January on top of everything else. Before you swipe, ask: will I still be paying for this at Easter? Trap two: the quick loan. A lender who isn't registered can cost far more than you think, and some will keep your bank card or your ID. The National Credit Regulator's advice: "borrow wisely from registered credit providers". You can check a lender on its website, ncr.org.za.

Full guide: "Festive Season on a Budget: How Not to Start January Broke (South Africa 2026)" on the Money From Zero channel.
